name: Adrianne Lenker
label: 4AD
lede: Adrianne Lenker wrote her first song at eight and made four Big Thief albums in four years. Then she set up in a woodland studio with a few friends, no drums and no screens.

eras.title: Fourteen homes by the age of eight
eras.text: Adrianne Lenker was born in Indianapolis and raised mostly in Minnesota, after her family left the religious group it had joined. At thirteen she was recording an album with her father as manager.

years.h: Born in Indianapolis, into a group her family left
years.p: Lenker's family left the Christian group it belonged to when she was about four, then moved through fourteen rented homes by the time she was eight.
years.xp:
At five, a railroad spike fell from a treehouse roof in Nisswa, Minnesota, and lodged in her skull. She survived, and later wrote about it in the Big Thief song "Mythological Beauty".

She was homeschooled and wrote her first song at eight. Per Wikipedia, she also took up karate hard enough to win the Minnesota state title three years running.

eras.title: A GED at sixteen, then Boston
eras.text: A teenage record, a GED and a scholarship took Lenker to Berklee, then to Brooklyn, where she ran into Buck Meek in a grocery store.

years.h: A fourteen-year-old puts out Stages of the Sun
years.p: The album came out on the small LucidTunes label on February 28. A live record, Live at the Southern, followed the same year.

years.h: Berklee, on a scholarship Susan Tedeschi funds
years.p: After a GED at sixteen, Lenker went to Berklee College of Music in Boston and met the guitarist [[Buck Meek|b8780175-4ff4-4d87-8e54-999f70dbb5ec]] at a concert.
years.xp: When Lenker moved to Brooklyn she ran into Meek again at Mr. Kiwi, a Bushwick grocery store, on the day she arrived. They started playing together, and Meek became a constant in her music.

eras.title: Self-released, then a band
eras.text: Lenker put out her own records, made one with Meek, and cut Big Thief's debut in a July session in upstate New York.

years.h: Hours Were the Birds comes out on her own
years.p: It was Lenker's second solo album. a-sides and b-sides, with Buck Meek, followed on May 1, and Saddle Creek reissued both on November 16, 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Masterpiece (Big Thief album) · Wikipedia: Adrianne Lenker
years.h: Big Thief cut Masterpiece beside Lake Champlain
years.p: Lenker, Buck Meek, bassist Max Oleartchik and drummer Jason Burger recorded in Essex, New York, with producer [[Andrew Sarlo|700b0a0c-9c3b-44b3-8de4-51c1a5f4b2e1]].
years.xp: Wikipedia credits [[James Krivchenia|611cb5a3-42cd-4aef-98e6-5749b88bf63a]] with engineering and additional production. He was first hired to engineer the debut and later replaced Burger on drums.

eras.title: An album a year
eras.text: Big Thief released a record every year while Lenker kept writing solo songs on the road, and the band left Saddle Creek for 4AD.

years.cap: Lenker with Big Thief at SXSW, Austin, March 2016
years.h: Big Thief's debut lands on Saddle Creek, with a toy dinosaur on the cover
years.p: Pitchfork's Jill Mapes gave Masterpiece a 7.7. The cover is a childhood photograph of Lenker's mother with a toy dinosaur.

years.cap: Big Thief on stage in Kingston, New York, June 22, 2017
yt: Big Thief live on KEXP, August 2017
years.h: A house-sat farmhouse in upstate New York becomes Capacity
years.p: The band recorded for about a month, with overdubs at Black Lodge in Brooklyn.

years.h: Abysskiss fits ten solo songs into 33 minutes
years.p: Recorded at Panoramic House in West Marin, California, with producer [[Luke Temple|27c978f2-284d-469f-a116-23f7fca9a6fc]]. "Terminal Paradise" and "From" came back with the full band on U.F.O.F.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Jayson Greene gave it 8 out of 10. Per Wikipedia, the album was built from songs Lenker wrote on tour with Big Thief.

years.h: Lenker and Buck Meek divorce, and the band carries on
years.p: The split came in 2018, and per Wikipedia the two stayed in Big Thief as close friends.

years.cap: Lenker at Haldern Pop Festival, Germany
years.h: Pitchfork gives U.F.O.F. a 9.2 and Best New Music
years.p: Big Thief's first album on 4AD was recorded in June 2018 at Bear Creek in Woodinville, Washington.

years.cap: Lenker at The National's Homecoming festival, Cincinnati
years.h: Five months later, Two Hands and a Grammy nomination for "Not"
years.p: Cut at Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas, with nearly all the vocals live. Pitchfork's Quinn Moreland called "Not" a towering statement.

eras.title: Alone in a one-room cabin
eras.text: A cancelled European tour sent Lenker to a cabin in Massachusetts, and the recordings became her first 4AD solo releases.

years.h: A month in a Westhampton cabin with an Otari tape machine
years.p: Lenker and engineer [[Philip Weinrobe|3d5aa701-6cad-4bfe-8e42-fde78fc7123d]] worked on a tape machine the pair got mid-session.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, each day opened and closed with improvised guitar pieces, which became instrumentals. The palette included a paintbrush and white pine needles, with rain, wind, a wood stove and birds on tape.

yt: Lenker solo, KEXP at Home, March 2021
years.h: songs and instrumentals arrive together on 4AD
years.p: Metacritic scored songs 84 from 19 reviews, with "Anything" and "Dragon Eyes" leading the way.
years.xp: The two albums came out together on October 23, 2020, and songs placed 11th on Pitchfork's 2020 list.

years.h: A camper in Joshua Tree stands in for the Tiny Desk
years.p: NPR's pandemic-era Tiny Desk (Home) series filmed Lenker inside a camper in Joshua Tree National Park.

eras.title: Back to the woods, with friends
eras.text: After a double album with the band, Lenker went into the woods again with Weinrobe and friends. Pitchfork put the result on its list of the year's 50 best.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
years.h: Big Thief cut 45 songs down to 20 for a double album
years.p: They tracked Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You in five locations from April to December 2020, and Pitchfork gave it 9.0.
years.xp: The album earned two Grammy nominations, for Best Alternative Music Album and, for "Certainty", Best Alternative Music Performance.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bright Future (Adrianne Lenker album) · Stereogum: Premature Evaluation
years.h: Nick Hakim, Mat Davidson and Josefin Runsteen join Lenker at Double Infinity
years.p: The Bright Future sessions ran in fall 2022 at a woodland studio in a 150-year-old New England building.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, nobody stopped a take, and Lenker did not listen back until the other players had left. Weinrobe is quoted: "Adrianne and I never once looked at a computer screen."

years.h: "Ruined" leads the way for Bright Future
years.p: The single came with an official video, and a live version with Nick Hakim followed from Greenwich Village.

years.cap: Lenker on stage at the Barbican, London, April 2024
years.h: A Bandcamp EP for the Palestine Children's Relief Fund
years.p: Lenker self-released I Won't Let Go of Your Hand, with proceeds going to the charity.

years.cap: Lenker solo at the Barbican, London, April 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Bright Future (Adrianne Lenker album) · Stereogum: Premature Evaluation
years.h: Bright Future has piano, banjo and violin, and no drums
years.p: Twelve songs in 43 minutes, recorded live to tape. Stereogum's Premature Evaluation singled out "Real House" and "Free Treasure", the latter co-written with James Krivchenia.
years.xp: The album was released on 4AD on March 22, 2024 and charted at No. 5 on the US Heat list and No. 18 on Folk, per Wikipedia. It earned Lenker her first solo Grammy nomination, for Best Folk Album.

years.big: "It feels like I'm following an invisible thread of intuition."
years.src: Album of the Year: Adrianne Lenker, Bright Future · Wikipedia: Bright Future (Adrianne Lenker album)
yt: Lenker plays "Free Treasure" on The Tonight Show
years.h: Pitchfork ranks Bright Future No. 23 for the year
years.p: Lenker, in her own words. Andy Cush's review scored the album 8.4, per Album of the Year.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the review as Best New Music, and Pitchfork ranked the album No. 23 on its list of the year's 50 best. Slant and The Vinyl Factory put it second in their year-end lists; Uncut placed it sixth.

years.h: Founding bassist Max Oleartchik leaves Big Thief
years.p: The band said he was out "for interpersonal reasons", and that the parting came with mutual respect.

eras.title: Back to the trio
eras.text: Lenker, Meek and James Krivchenia made the first Big Thief album without Max Oleartchik.

years.cap: Lenker at Way Out West, Gothenburg
years.h: Big Thief makes Double Infinity as a trio, with guests
years.p: Dom Monks produced at Power Station in New York, with ten session players including Laraaji. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
